title: Example 14-2: Cast of Characters with Fonts

illustrates.quote: Retain font attributes on speaker names; omit font attributes on speaker identifications.

blocks.features: Character names (Lucentio, Gremio, Hortensio) are in bold font, separated from their identifications by a wide, columnar space (no punctuation between name and identification). Identifications are in regular font.

print.printFeatures: Cast list with bold character names; identifications in plain font.

braille.notes: 1-3 margins for the cast of characters (14.2.1b); the bold indicator (^1) precedes each character name only (14.2.1c: retain font attributes on speaker names, omit on identifications); a single space (not the print's own wide column gap) separates name from identification, per 14.2.1d (no punctuation shown in print, so none inserted, and no extra spacing indicated either).

resolution: A/B agreed on braille (byte-for-byte) and on the substance of print.blocks (both left the bold markup out of item.text itself, instead describing it only in a prose features string that buildModel14 cannot consume). Per this repo's own established convention (every other gold section marks emphasis in place with Emboss's **bold**/*italic* cell-markup DSL directly in a block's text, not as a side-channel description — see gold-run.mjs's own header comment), item.text was rewritten here to carry **Lucentio** etc. directly. Forward-translated through Emboss's translator (buildModel14's 'cast-list' -> {type:'play', subtype:'prose', segments} blocks, 1-3 margins, bold segment on the name only): EXACT MATCH against this braille (see differences.md).
